response.overview: When everyday objects are detached from their original context and function, they fall into a transitional state between the familiar and the unfamiliar. Their pure objecthood—once concealed by functionality—becomes open to close observation. The camera, in a composed and detached gaze, observes these objects as they move or remain still within an uninhabited space, allowing them to resemble a form of spontaneous dialogue. Through the visual combination of transitional spaces and objects stripped of functionality, the work depicts the psychological state of individuals confronting order, isolation, and uncertainty within enclosed structures. Using low-light imagery, a film-like texture, and objects arranged in stillness or perpetual motion, it creates a sensory atmosphere suspended between reality and dream.
response.title: Vessel of Inversion
